correctness.rationale: From exact Sylow counts of A5 and uniqueness of Sylow subgroups in nilpotent N, recover the compensation equation. New-prime gains from seven distinct primes are at most 29/63. All larger old-prime defects exceed this; the sole possible one is 4/9 from order-two Sylow-2. Six new primes cannot reach 4/9. Five rows of exact forced-prime bounds eliminate skipped and higher-power choices; the remaining sixth prime is 23 or 29 and both final denominators are nonintegral. Published nine-prime witness attains the bound. Eight-prime gain bound gives the equality-case old-prime rigidity. CHECK.py verifies all exact fractions.
